subject: Marine science
imageAlt: A sea turtle swimming above a coral reef in sunlit blue water
summary: Reef ecosystems, the organisms in them, food and shelter, and conservation.
worldSummary: Predict, change the conditions, observe the results, and explain what happened.
intro: Built on the Ocean Explorer world already used with students. Learn how a reef works, then go in and test it.
topics: What it takes to protect a reef
objectives: Identify key living and nonliving parts of a reef ecosystem.
Explain a relationship between organisms and their environment.
Predict a plausible effect of a specified change to the ecosystem.
Use evidence to explain an ecosystem relationship.

lessons.title: Meet the ecosystem
lessons.activity: Short introduction, a labeled visual, and a guided observation.

lessons.title: Explore relationships
lessons.activity: A guided task in Ocean Explorer, or an equivalent text-and-visual activity.

lessons.title: Investigate a change
lessons.activity: A scenario prompt, then exploration or a structured alternative.

lessons.title: Apply and reflect
lessons.activity: A final scenario and a short reflection.

access: Runs in your web browser — no install.
Every world activity will have an accessible alternative that keeps the same objective.

subject: Earth & space
imageAlt: A satellite with extended solar panels orbiting above the curve of the Earth
summary: Satellites, orbital infrastructure, and how we observe Earth from space.
worldSummary: Explore Earth and its satellites in 3D, on desktop or in WebXR, then solve real scenarios.

subject: Electricity
imageAlt: A miniature city with wind turbines, roads, and a bridge at sunset
summary: How power is generated, moved, and delivered, and how supply meets demand.
worldSummary: Build a neighborhood's grid, balance supply and demand, and restore power when things change.
